description: Provider-neutral AI vocabulary for a future AI Foundation, plus the first provider adapters behind the declared seams (P2.25). The vocabulary declares shapes; the adapters translate one explicitly configured external provider each onto the canonical contract through an injected transport. No default provider, no vendor SDK, no stored credential, no new dependency.
notImplemented: No LLM inference of any kind is performed by LEGO itself — every token comes from an external provider reached through an explicitly configured adapter transport; no canned completion ever stands in for a provider.

No default model gateway client and no vendor SDK. The P2.25 model provider adapter speaks only through an injected exchange binding, configuration is explicit, and credentials are supplied per call — never stored, defaulted or echoed. 9Router remains an example of a provider kind only.

No default tool gateway client. The P2.25 tool provider adapter binds declared tools behind the same injected-transport, per-call-authorization boundary; Composio remains an example of a provider kind only.

No owned or bundled agent runtime. External agent runtimes are adapted behind the P2.21 seam (P2.25 ships the first real external runtime binding), never reimplemented — Hermes, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenClaw and DeepSeek remain examples of runtime kinds.
No MCP server and no MCP client.
No ambient network call, no daemon, no background process and no new dependency: transports exist only at the explicitly configured adapter edge.

No GitHub client and no standing GitHub token: GitHub and every application provider are integration boundaries reached only through explicitly handed-over, scoped, request-bound authorization — never a stored credential, never a global repository authority, never implicit account discovery (P2.26).

No provider discovery and no automatic provider selection: a provider exists in the system only where its declaration profile (sim/local/cloud) was made explicitly — absence is the honest not-configured state, never a default (P2.26).
vendorRule: A vendor name may appear in this file ONLY inside an `examples` array, and only as an illustration of a provider kind. No vendor may appear in an id, a required field, a code path or a default. If a vendor name is ever needed to make a contract work, the contract is wrong.

taxonomy.rule: These five concepts are deliberately distinct. Conflating them is the single most common way an AI integration becomes unreplaceable, because it welds a capability to one vendor's transport.

concepts.capability: WHAT the system can do. Owned by a LEGO. Stable. Example: `agent.session`.
concepts.implementation: HOW a capability is realised. Swappable. Example: a JS implementation or a Rust implementation.
concepts.provider: WHERE an implementation is sourced from. Example kinds: model-provider, tool-provider, application-provider.
concepts.transport: HOW bytes move. Example: in-process, worker, http, mcp.
concepts.runtime: WHERE an agent or system executes. Example kinds: agent-runtime, simulation-runtime.

taxonomy.layering: capability -> contract -> operations -> interaction -> implementation -> provider -> transport -> runtime
taxonomy.antiPattern: Declaring `composio.github.repo.read` as a capability. That fuses capability (repo read), provider (Composio) and application (GitHub) into one identifier that cannot be replaced without a rename.

model-provider.summary: Supplies inference. Text, embeddings, possibly tool-calling.
examples: a hosted model gateway such as 9Router

tool-provider.summary: Supplies callable tools and readable resources to an agent.
examples: a tool/app gateway such as Composio

application-provider.summary: An external application exposed as capabilities. Independent of whichever gateway reaches it.

agent-runtime.summary: Executes an agent session. Owns the agent loop, not the model.

simulation-runtime.summary: Executes a scenario or simulation rather than a task-directed agent.

providerProfiles.rule: Provider declarations are EXPLICIT: declared, not assumed. No hidden discovery, no automatic provider selection, no standing provider authority, no stored credential — configuration remains explicit on the P2.25 adapters and the absence of a declaration is the honest not-configured state, never a default.

sim.summary: A simulated/fixture provider declared for offline and test execution.
sim.authority: simulation authority only — never reaches an external service
sim.configRule: explicit declaration required; sim never becomes a fallback for an undeclared provider

local.summary: A provider running on the same host, reached through an explicitly named local endpoint.
local.authority: local processes are still explicitly declared — no process or port discovery
local.configRule: explicit declaration required; local never implies trusted or standing

cloud.summary: A remotely hosted provider reached over the network through an explicitly configured endpoint.
cloud.authority: remote authority stays at the adapter edge; credentials are handed over per call, never stored
cloud.configRule: explicit declaration required; cloud never implies an account, a token or an auto-selected vendor

modelGateway.rule: Provider-neutral. An implementation maps these operations onto whatever the provider actually speaks.

modelMetadata.rule: Cost and latency are OPTIONAL and may be absent or stale. A consumer must treat a missing value as unknown, never as zero. A router that reads absent cost as free will always pick the unpriced model.

modelGateway.streamRule: `stream` must declare a backpressure policy. `block` is the default because a token stream a consumer cannot keep up with should slow the producer, not accumulate in memory.

toolGateway.rule: Tool-shaped, not vendor-shaped. MCP is one possible transport adapter, never the internal model.

toolMetadata.rule: `sideEffects` is REQUIRED and one of read-only | writes | destructive | external. It drives the approval contract. A tool that does not declare its side effects must be treated as destructive, because the safe default for an unknown effect is the most restrictive one.

applicationProvider.rule: An application is modelled by its capabilities, independent of the path used to reach it. The same application may be reachable natively AND through a tool gateway; both are providers of the same capabilities.
applicationProvider.firstClassRule: A native integration must never be forced through a gateway. GitHub access via a direct native provider and GitHub access via a tool gateway are two provider bindings of ONE capability set, and the native path must remain available with no gateway configured.

exampleCapabilities.note: Illustrative capability decomposition. No GitHub client is implemented here.

handedOverAccess.rule: Application integration access (GitHub is the canonical example) is an integration boundary, not a privileged Core capability: access is explicitly handed over, scoped to declared capability words, and request-bound by a requestId.
handoff: grantReference (opaque reference, never a raw credential)
handedOverAccess.replaceable: the GitHub integration must remain replaceable and must not become a built-in dependency of every plugin
handedOverAccess.decides: ai.approval decides the grant; the handoff proves well-formedness only — configuration is never authority

agentRuntime.rule: A runtime-neutral agent lifecycle that an external runtime can satisfy without any core change. This is the contract Hermes, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and others could implement; none is implemented here.

supports.session: boolean — can it hold a multi-turn session
supports.background: boolean — can it keep working after the caller disconnects
supports.stream: boolean — can it emit incremental output
supports.cancellation: boolean — can it actually stop, or only be abandoned
supports.delegation: boolean — can it spawn child agents

runtimeMetadata.rule: `supports.cancellation: false` is a legitimate, declarable answer. A runtime that cannot stop must say so, because the alternative is a cancel that silently does nothing while the caller believes work stopped.

agentRuntime.pauseRule: pause/resume are optional. A runtime that cannot pause declares it and answers `lego.operation_unsupported` rather than faking a pause by buffering output.

agentSession.rule: Session state is identity plus references. Transcripts, contexts and artifacts are referenced, never inlined, so session state stays small enough to persist cheaply and to survive a storage backend change.
agentSession.sizeRule: A session record must remain bounded. Storing a transcript inside it would make session size grow without limit and would put model output into the same row as control state — see the artifact contract.

agentMachine.rule: The bounded execution FOUNDATION of the Agent Machine: one canonical state machine for machine, agent and task identity, lifecycle (incl. ready), step bookkeeping, budgets, bounded delegation bookkeeping, bounded graph validation and deterministic transitions. It is a foundation, not an engine: nothing in P2.16 executes a step, runs a model or calls a tool, and delegation is bookkeeping metadata only — never child execution or permission inheritance. The future full loop (ai.agent-runtime) builds on this contract.
agentMachine.executorKindRule: A kind is a declaration, not an authority. The provider must explicitly support the requested kind; the core never infers shell, filesystem, process or remote execution from it.
agentMachine.referenceRule: Context, Session, Memory and Workspace are consumed by opaque reference only (contextReference, sessionReference, workspaceReference). Agent Machine never redefines or drives their lifecycles, and Memory is deliberately not referenced at all.
agentMachine.stateRule: The canonical agent vocabulary quoted from the AI set and ai.agent-session@1.0.0, plus the machine-level ready state added by agentMachine.prepare in 1.1.0. waiting is entered only by an approval-required step and left only by cancel: approval resolution belongs to the fail-closed ai.approval contract, not to P2.16.
agentMachine.budgetRule: Budgets are first-class, declared at create, clamped to bounded ceilings and always positive. There is no unlimited mode; exhaustion is a stable error and a stable terminal failure (budget-exhausted). maxChildren bounds delegation edges (undeclared = 0) and maxTasksPerAgent bounds machines per agent identity.
agentMachine.concurrencyRule: Every mutation carries expectedVersion (optimistic concurrency). Stale or duplicate step submissions are deterministic conflicts, never silent reorders.
agentMachine.providerSeam: replaceable; InMemoryAgentMachineProvider is the bounded default. The provider stores opaque records only and never receives work to execute.
implementationBoundary: bounded identity (machineId, agentId, taskId — three distinct forms)
explicit lifecycle (incl. ready via prepare) and deterministic transitions
bounded step bookkeeping with sequence and identity rules
first-class execution budgets (incl. maxChildren and maxTasksPerAgent)
bounded delegation bookkeeping with narrowed, clamped edges (no inheritance)
deterministic, session-scoped Universal Agent Event derivation
notImplemented: the agent loop or any autonomous runtime
delegation execution, child-agent spawning or multi-agent runtime orchestration (bookkeeping edges only)
parallel execution runtime, fan-out or fan-in scheduling (graph representation only)
stream, send, artifact and close operations
shell, filesystem, process or network authority
agentMachine.capabilityScopeRule: capabilityScope is a bounded list validated against the lego-foundation capability registry; unknown ids, duplicates and overlong lists fail closed. Delegation grants are an explicit narrowed subset of this scope — never inherited, never widened.
agentMachine.graphRule: Execution graphs are bounded representation: sequential, parallel, branch, fan-out, fan-in, join and retry with at most 128 nodes, 16 dependencies per node and 8 retry attempts. Cycles, dangling refs, multi-entry graphs and permission-bearing nodes are rejected. Validation never executes and never mutates the input.
agentMachine.eventRule: Six session-scoped derived event types (agent.created/started/delegated/completed/failed/cancelled). Deterministic, sanitized, reference-only: no payload, no secret, no hidden reasoning, no transport emission.

delegation.rule: Delegation is a graph edge with an explicit, NARROWED authority grant.
delegation.authorityRule: A child receives only capabilities explicitly listed in `grantedCapabilities`, and that list must be a SUBSET of the parent's. Parent authority never propagates automatically. Automatic propagation means one delegation chain quietly ends in an agent holding every permission in the system.

budget.rule: A budget is required. An unbudgeted delegation can recurse until a resource limit stops it, which on a low-end device means the device stops.

delegation.deadlineRule: A child deadline is clamped to the parent's, exactly as the operation envelope already clamps derived deadlines.

events.rule: One authoritative event vocabulary. Events are small, structured and reference-based.

envelope.rule: `summary` is a short operational string. `references` point at artifacts, contexts and traces.

events.privacyRule: No event may carry hidden chain-of-thought, raw prompts, credentials or full model output. An event says what happened and where the detail lives. Reasoning traces are not an audit format and storing them creates a liability with no operational benefit.
events.sizeRule: Events are capped and reference-based. Large payloads go to the artifact contract.

decision.rule: An auditable operational rationale, not a reasoning transcript.
decision.privacyRule: `reasonSummary` is a concise operational justification. Private chain-of-thought must NOT be stored. The auditable question is what was chosen and on what evidence, not what the model internally considered.

approval.rule: Fail-closed. An action requiring approval does not proceed on timeout, on error, or on a missing approver.
approval.failClosedRule: An expired or unanswered approval is a DENY. Defaulting to allow would make the safety layer disappear exactly when the system is under stress or unattended.
approval.notBuilt: No approval UI, no approval store and no enforcement middleware exists. This declares the shape a future safety layer must satisfy.

artifact.rule: Reference-based. Large data never travels inside an event or a session record.
artifact.storageRule: `storageRef` is an opaque reference resolved by the storage domain. The AI contracts must not know whether it is a local file, SQLite row or object store — that is exactly the abstraction the storage domain owns.

context.rule: Hierarchical and selectively loadable. An agent loads the narrowest scope that answers its question.
context.selectiveLoadRule: There is no mandatory load-everything context. Requiring the whole instance as context makes cost scale with instance size instead of task size, which fails first on exactly the low-end devices this project targets.
context.compactionRule: Compaction must emit `context.compacted` and preserve the checksum chain, so a later reader can tell that what it is reading is a reduction rather than the original.
context.securityRule: Context state rejects credentials, tokens, secrets, cookies, private model reasoning, raw hidden prompts, arbitrary host paths and unrestricted capability grants. References are preferred over payloads.

memory.rule: Persistent knowledge that survives context replacement. Context is what is loaded now; Session tracks continuity; Memory is what is intentionally retained. Loading memory into context is always an explicit, bounded caller choice.
memory.referencesRule: Each reference declares an id and a graph edge relation from the memory vocabulary; linkage is explicit and never auto-dereferenced.
memory.retentionRule: Retention is an explicit declaration; EPHEMERAL and WORKING are candidates for forgetting, IMPORTANT/DURABLE/PERMANENT persist until an explicit forget.
memory.loadRule: Never dump full memory into context. Retrieval is deterministic, scoped, ordered by creation time and bounded by the caller's limit. Relevance ranking is deferred; list returns a deterministic page.
memory.providerNote: Obsidian is a Memory Provider / human knowledge interface adapter. It is NOT the internal source of truth, and the memory graph must remain valid with no provider connected.
implementationBoundary: bounded in-memory provider behind the provider boundary
content and reference validation with sensitive rejection
scope-isolated retrieval with deterministic ordering and pagination
notImplemented: vector search, embeddings or relevance-ranked traversal
Agent Machine loop, Workspace or Runtime Adapter runtime
memory.securityRule: Memory content and references reject credentials, secrets, tokens, host paths and transcripts by name and pattern. Checksum mismatches are reported, never silently repaired.

resourceProfiles.rule: Resource metadata describes requirements. It is not a scheduler and grants no enforcement.

profiles.low-resource: Runs on a phone, a Termux session or a 1GB VPS. No GPU, no persistent daemon, minimal memory.
profiles.standard: A normal laptop or small server.
profiles.high-resource: Needs substantial CPU or memory; not assumable on a user device.
profiles.remote: Executes elsewhere. Local cost is a network call; availability becomes a real failure mode.

resourceProfiles.noLocalInstallRule: No external runtime may become a local installation requirement. Every AI provider is optional and remotely satisfiable, because requiring a local agent runtime would exclude the low-end targets the foundation explicitly supports.

zeroInstall.rule: AI Foundation present with NO provider configured is a VALID, fully supported system state — not an error and not a degraded install.
zeroInstall.reportedAs: capability-unavailable with reason 'no inference provider configured'
zeroInstall.honestyRule: The system must never fake inference, never return a canned completion and never pretend a provider exists. It reports that the foundation is ready and no provider is connected. A fake answer is worse than no answer, because the user cannot tell it is fake.
zeroInstall.why: This is what allows a provider such as a model gateway to be connected later as configuration rather than as an architectural change.

mcp.rule: MCP is an interoperability ADAPTER at the edge. It must never become the internal application architecture.
mcp.boundary: external world <-> MCP adapter <-> LEGO capability contract <-> implementation

roles.mcp-server: Exposes selected n8n capabilities to external MCP clients. An explicit export list, never the whole registry.
roles.mcp-client: Consumes an external MCP server as a tool-provider implementation.

mcp.internalRule: No internal LEGO may call another LEGO over MCP. Internal communication stays CALL/EVENT/STREAM/BATCH over the local dispatcher, as ADR-0004 requires.
mcp.mappingRule: MCP concepts map ONTO the tool gateway contract; the tool gateway is not defined in MCP terms. If MCP changes, one adapter changes.
mcp.exportRule: Capabilities are exported explicitly and individually. There is no export-everything switch, because the set of capabilities safe to hand to an external client is never the full set.
mcp.stateRule: declared = known as a declaration, with no authority implied; permission-required = known but not exposed until an explicit permission/approval decision; exposed = explicitly exposed after the permission gate passes; blocked = prohibited, unknown, invalid or denied. Exposure and Agent Control authority are separate dimensions: neither ever implies the other.
permissionGate: has an explicit permission/approval grant been presented?
exposed — any unknown or invalid condition is blocked
mcp.authorityRule: MCP exposure never implies Agent Control authority, and Agent Control authority never implies MCP exposure. A declared server is not a trusted server; a declared capability is not an exposed capability; an exposed capability grants no agent permission. Every boundary transition is explicit: no export-everything switch, no inference from names, descriptions, transports, server identities or provider names.
mcp.failClosedRule: Unknown server, unknown capability, unknown permission claims and invalid inputs fail closed to blocked (or are rejected as contract violations when the input itself is malformed). A pending, expired, scope-mismatched or identity-mismatched approval never exposes: only an explicit granted ai.approval decision can.
mcp.approvalRule: A capability that declares requiresApproval or requiresPermission is satisfied only by presenting an ai.approval reference whose decision is granted with matching identity and scope (ai.approval@1.0.0, P2.19). Agent permissions are never accepted as evidence at this boundary.
mcp.notBuilt: No MCP server, client, adapter or dependency exists in this repository.

transportRouting.rule: Transport is selected by locality, never by habit. The business contract does not change when the transport does.
transportRouting.prohibition: Never force every call through HTTP. An HTTP hop between two objects in one process is the most expensive available way to call a function.
transportRouting.carryRule: A transport advertises which interaction classes it can carry. The OPERATION owns its interaction class; a transport that cannot carry it is simply not eligible. A transport must never silently downgrade a STREAM to a CALL — the caller asked for incremental output and would instead wait for a single late response.

rustPolicy.rule: Rust remains an implementation choice beneath these contracts, exactly as ADR-0005 states.
rustPolicy.appliesTo: Any AI Foundation component may later have a JS implementation and a Rust implementation under the same contract, selected by configuration.
rustPolicy.prohibition: No Rust is written in this phase. Rust is never chosen merely to demonstrate that Rust exists, and must never require a compiler on an end-user device.
rustPolicy.contractPreservation: A Rust implementation must satisfy the identical contract, operations and interaction classes. If it needs a different contract, it is a different capability and must be justified as one.

workspaceBoundary.rule: Workspace integration preserves the existing Workspace contract: ai.workspace@1.0.0 keeps its identity, metadata, opaque resource-reference and lifecycle model. Workspace internals are never moved into AI Foundation, no second Workspace implementation is created, and no integration boundary introduces unrestricted filesystem, shell or subprocess authority.
never: workspace internals moved into AI Foundation
